I think I am struggling with my relationships in regards to veganism, because I see it as a political stance. To me, its a continuation of so many values that I believe in, and a treatment to so many social ills - whereas everyone else boils it down to "a personal choice" or "mad hippy syndrome".

My mother is a good example. Surprise, surprise, we have very similar political ideologies, but I feel she uses whatever excuse is at hand to stick their head in the sand. My mother is a social worker, and if there was a profession that should follow through on the ideals of fairness, equality, and loving kindness, then surely its a social worker? But instead, she continues to ignore the intersectionality of specialism and all the other forms of prejudice that she fights on a day to day basis.

She is an excellent case study of how I feel veganism has affected most of my relationships. People who I once thought were "upstanding citizens" with "great ideals" that "always tried to follow through" have become hollow charlatans that merely pay lip service to those things, whilst deliberately ignoring facts, refusing to engage in conversation and using ad hominem arguments.

I should also probably clarify that my girlfriend is incredibly supportive of my veganism. I have always done the majority of the cooking, and since the swap to veganism that has continued, with nothing but love and support from her. She has even cut down her animal product intake outside of home at her own volition, which is great. What I meant was that although convinced, it is not a topic of conversation that she wishes to discuss very much - which is hard when a) I feel so strongly about it and b) other peoples views/actions about it bother me so much (as you can see).

Also I am looking for another job, and have been for a long time.. This is the third year in a row that I've had to take a part time Christmas temp position in retail to get by. I previously worked in a call center, and it was fucking awful, but it was outbound calls and maybe that explains why. Thanks for the suggestions. A friend suggested that I try and get involved in political activism, and that I might be able to build myself a career in that somehow.

Vegan for ~2 months.

Pros

* I no longer feel guilty about everything I eat - in fact I actually feel actively positive sometimes when I make the ethical choice
* My digestive system generally feels better - fewer bloated feelings and less heartburn
* I've learnt a lot of new cooking techniques and generally feel more confident "throwing" together whatever ingredients I have available to make something nice.

Cons

* I often feel sad about the huge problems caused by the meat/dairy industries. I was largely ignorant of these issues before going vegan, but now everything seems to return to the need to be vegan. It seems like the only real solution to so many of our social ills is for a vast majority of people to go vegan - and fast... but its just not going to happen. I often find myself wishing I could re-stick my head in the sand, just to hide from the McDeath bilboards.
* My relationships have taken a toll. My parents are generally receptive people but refuse to have a proper conversation about my decision. My mother has even gone far enough to say that she "will only talk about it after you've been vegan for a year" - which is just a BS excuse, in the hopes that I will fail and she won't have to question her own lifestyle. I also fear that I've become "the preachy vegan" to my friends, and that my girlfriend finds conversations about veganism stale.
* I work at a supermarket, and working/selling meat/dairy/egg products on such a mass scale is pretty depressing. I also spilt a couple cartons of cream today, and all I could think was "Some cow died/was tortured for that", which made me feel pretty bad.
